gen-gf-sniglet-gf-el-messiri: El Messiri reads modern and tidy, with a faint wedge of pen pressure in every curve and a wide slot in its c. Sniglet is the blunt, level one; El Messiri does the finer work.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-electrolize: Sniglet leads with rounded terminals that stop short of curling back. Electrolize follows with an open-jawed c like pliers, and its low, plain stroke contrast lets a longer stretch move along without any pulse tugging at the eye.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-elms-sans: Sniglet stops its terminals short of curling back in, giving a level, quiet beat with no weight accents. Elms Sans is the strongest counterpart here: a ballpoint-plain line with a see-through gap in each s.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-exo: Bent tubing is what Sniglet's letterforms look like, rounded and distinctive. Exo supplies the strongest quality of the pair, wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp beside that quiet, level display.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-exo-2: Sniglet looks like spaghetti laid out in letters, one flat line with no weight accents. Exo 2 then carries a longer passage easily, its curves full of daylight and its plain sans manner clean and businesslike.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-faculty-glyphic: Round, blunt and unshaded, Sniglet draws flat strokes that stop short of curling back in. And Faculty Glyphic, a plain sans with clear openings in its rounded letters, gives the body room; a bit more size for it would not hurt.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-fahkwang: Fahkwang reads soft and approachable, its round letters showing a faint nib pressure. Sniglet holds a calm, unvarying weight from word to word up top, while the sans below lets its bowls swell only slightly at their widest.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-figtree: Approachable first of all, Sniglet stops its terminals short of curling back in and keeps a quiet, level beat. Figtree, drawn as if with a marker tip and an e with a wide terminal gap, does the sans-serif reading work.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-finlandica: Finlandica reads clean and contemporary, with open-mouthed e crossbars and an outline of constant width you could trace with a finger. Its strongest quality is that clarity against Sniglet's blunt display.
gen-gf-sniglet-gf-fustat: Sniglet's terminals stop short of curling back in, level and unaccented. Fustat then reads easily over a longer passage, its lines like bent rope and a wide, clear gap where each c ends.
